Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement SOE reforms strengthened. Indicator: Report prepared, identifying and assessing the legitimacy and cost of community service obligations for at least 10 selected SOEs (2017 baseline: not prepared) Progress/Status: Report prepared, identifying and assessing legitimacy and cost of CSOs for at least nine selected SOEs Training to SOEMU (April 2024) on how to complete the FS from the trial balances and how to use the templates with GASB notes, all aiming to assist selected SOEs to complete FY23 soonest and as requested by the auditors, to provide more information, including draft FS and notes rather than just a reconciled trial balance
Work completed (April 2024) on the Proposal for Amendments to the SOE Act and Regulations
Ongoing support to SOEMU regarding following up on progress with each SOE relative to the status of their financial reporting and audit
Multiple templates to assist SOEs in preparing planning and reporting document
Assistance to selected SOEs with planning and reporting
Multiple training programs on compliance with the SOE Act delivered plus training on planning, governance and related topics
Several ‘How to' user manuals on planning, governance, monitoring and CSOs, have been provided,
Detailed work on identifying CSOs and first CSO agreement for MAWC
SOE Reform Roadmap prepared,
SOE Performance Report and Forecasting Reports provided in draft (yet to be authorized and circulated
Draft SOE CSO report and draft SOE Diagnostic report to be reviewed Draft SOE CSO report
Reviewing of Ministry plans to align with the format of SOE plans (ongoing). (Drafts are yet to be submitted to Minister and Secretary. Drafts will be submitted on May 16th, 2025
Draft Shared Services Proposal for SOEs (draft is complete however it is yet to be submitted to Minister and Secretary. Proposal to be submitted on May 16th, 2025)
Reviewing of Ministry plans to align with the format of SOE plans (ongoing). Data Source: SOEMU report Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement SOE reforms strengthened. Indicator: SOE monitoring unit established in MOF and staffed (2017 baseline: not established) Progress/Status: SOEMU remains operational and fully staffed, however search for replacement for SOEMU manager underway. Data Source: Cabinet or ministerial decision, or equivalent Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: At least 10 training sessions per year provided by the RCU, with women accounting for at least 40% of trainees (2017 baseline: training not provided) Progress/Status:  RCU continues to provide hands-on assistance and guidance in audit management to the core team formed by the MOF to handle the ongoing expedited audits, with the goal of completing audit of 1 fiscal year every 6 months until all audits are caught up with the completion of FY26 by June 2027. Data Source: Biannual progress reporting by the RCU Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: At least 20 road map reforms implemented, as per updated PFM Reform Roadmap action plan Progress/Status:  At least 20 road map reforms implemented, as per updated PFM Reform Roadmap action plan  Ongoing work on the RMI Financial Sector Development Plan in coordination with the RMI Banking Commission with the establishment of the Monetary Authority.  Annual Economic Policy Statement and submitted for inclusion with the FY2026 budget  Will be updated for any supplemental budget submitted during Nitijela session in 2026)  Ongoing alignment of FMIS budget coding with NSP linking annual budgets to NSP/FMIS and SDGs, this is critical to development of newly required Annual Implementation Plans (AIP) and Performance Reports as part of the new Fiscal Procedures Agreement (FPA)  Ongoing consultations to draft the NSP Five-year review and updating status of NSP KPIs.  To be presented to the donor's roundtable in Feb 2026  First draft of Budget Investment Framework and update report submitted November 2025. Preparing 2nd draft and report for submission February 2026. Final to be completed end of March 20206.  Ongoing consultations with Compact Ministries to review and finalize he BIF as per Amended Compact requirement  Strengthened asset management and development of Fixed Asset Management Manual Review of the FMIS Asset Management Module is ongoing and it will be fully utilized once necessary steps are done with the support technical personnel who will be hired by MOF  Ongoing work regarding performance-based management framework. Initial performance agreements signed and ongoing with critical agencies. As per the FPA performance reporting is required for Compact and Trust Fund reporting. Reporting frameworks continue to be evaluated and revised to ensure reporting meets all FPA requirements.  Assisting in the ongoing FY2023 audit conclusion work. EY to issue the Final Audited Financial Statements and Compliance Report on January 29, 2026  Complete the ongoing closing of the FY2024 financial books of the national government. Target to submit the FY24 FS package for audit on February 2, 2026.  Review underway of the FRDM currently used for guidance in the annual budget process including updating the Economic Policy Statement (EPS)  The RCU is assisting the WB PFM team in getting the Change Request II for system enhancements signed covering priority areas as identified by PFM-RCU, Data Source: Certification by MOF (by means of cabinet orders, government decisions, MOF memoranda, as appropriate), and corroborated by development partners Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: Revised fiscal responsibility bill approved by the PFM Reform Steering Committee (2018 baseline: Not revised) Progress/Status: Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Management Act and related regulations were enacted effective 8 June 2021.
Legislation currently used for guidance in regard to the annual budget process including updating the Economic Policy Statement (EPS); EPS updated annually.
Coordination with WB PFM project on review. Data Source: Committee decision Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: A dedicated officer-in- charge of the nontax revenue unit is appointed by the MOF to formulate policies and guidelines, develop databases and information systems, and review and rebase current fees and charges, among others. (2020 baseline: no officer-in-charge) Progress/Status: TBD with MOF Secretary and Management Staff. Data Source: Cabinet or ministerial decision, or equivalent Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: Draft legislation on contingent liabilities submitted by the PFM Reform Steering Committee (2020 baseline: not drafted) Progress/Status: The GRMI currently does not record any contingent liability. Loan guarantee arrangements are carried as outright Loans Payable with corresponding Advances on the financial books. To be discussed further with MOF management and EY. Data Source: Committee decision Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: Draft tax administration legislation submitted to PFM Reform Steering Committee (2020 baseline: only reform impacts analysis conducted—2020) Progress/Status:  Firm selected for implementation of new tax management Integrated Revenue Administration System (IRAS) for tax management. Contract expected to be signed by February 2026. system completed  Expect IRAS implantation by October 2026  Legislation drafted in July and passed in August Nitijela session. Phase 1 implementation beginning now for FY26 (PFTAC/IMF Technical Assistance)  In early 2024, the RMI government proposed a two-phased approach for adopting tax reforms to provide immediate relief to lower and disadvantaged income groups and address recent cost of living increases.  Phase 1 was passed by the Nitijela on September 26 2024  The second phase was passed by Nitijela in August 2025 to be effective October 2026. Data Source: Committee decision Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: Gender-responsive performance-based budgeting frameworks for 5 targeted local government units introduced, with inclusion of gender indicators (2020 baseline: none introduced) Progress/Status: Selection of local governments to be completed by February 2026 with work to begin later in 2026. (No change)
Data Source: Biannual progress reporting by the RCU Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: Complete financial statements and related schedules are submitted to the auditor and other stakeholders of the Government of the Marshall Islands (2023 baseline: MOF submits only the trial balance to the auditor during annual audit) Progress/Status: FY2024 closing activities are ongoing, with the aim to submit system-generated Funds Financial Statements (discussion with Bisan ongoing to fix remaining issues) and the Disclosure Notes.
RCU is also actively involved in all discussions concerning future submission by the MOF of the government-wide financial statements, with all key partners primarily the WB PFM team. Data Source: Biannual progress reporting by the RCU Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: Digitized fixed asset registry (inventory management, monitoring, and disposal of assets) completed by the Asset Management Unit. Assessment and valuation of unregistered assets and revaluation of old registered assets completed (2023 baseline: Fixed asset register manually prepared. Valuation and revaluation of assets not yet started) Progress/Status: Some progress achieved in implementing the Fixed Assets Management Manual starting with the ongoing identification of property coordinators across the government including from the overseas missions. This will allow the GRMI to pursue a decentralized approach on asset management with a lead Asset Manager from the MOF.
MOF is hiring a support technical personnel to assist in the inventory management and in the administration of the Asset Management Module which is available in the MOF FMIS. Data Source: Biannual progress reporting by the RCU Actual value:

Output: MOF's institutional capacity to implement the PFM Reform Roadmap strengthened. Indicator: Human resource reform initiatives implemented to reduce employee turnover rate within the MOF by 3 percentage points and to better equip the MOF in handling disruptions because of unavoidable staff departures (2023 baseline: (10% turnover as of January 2023, with no formal backup system or onboarding and offboarding system in place) Progress/Status: Ongoing coordination with WB PFM project and MOF HR Officer. Data Source: MOF's annual project progress reports Actual value:
